question: After independent maximum-visible view selection produced zero reference cycles, does ranking consumed PV28 frame pairs by mutually visible registered physical target surface expose a stronger transport opportunity without RGB or model access?

surface_correspondence.method: Mutual nearest target-mesh vertices after the official rescan-to-reference transform.

ranking: Maximize mutually corresponding physical target vertices that are depth-consistent visible in both frames; ties prefer aligned view direction, stronger minimum short side and depth visibility, then earlier frames.

literature_motivation.source: Sattler et al., Improving Image-Based Localization by Active Correspondence Search, ECCV 2012
literature_motivation.use: Prioritize correspondence opportunities using covisibility instead of treating views independently.

literature_motivation.source: Jiang et al., R-SCoRe supplementary, CVPR 2025
literature_motivation.use: Frustum overlap and covisibility graphs can approximate matchable image relationships without feature-model selection.

literature_motivation.source: Learning Where to Look: Self-supervised Viewpoint Selection for Active Localization, 2024
literature_motivation.use: Active localization should select viewpoints for localization quality, not visibility alone.

next_action: If the selected pair materially increases jointly visible registered target surface over frames 92/111, freeze that one pair for one consumed-source unchanged-carrier Development replay; otherwise abandon this selector.
claim_boundary: This consumed-source geometry/depth diagnostic can rank joint physical-surface visibility only. It is not RGB correspondence evidence, confirmation, exact-instance binding, named entrance, ownership, access, traversability, waypoint, arrival, handoff, benefit, reliability or safety.
